schema: Each row is one venue or product that prices private-company valuations. settlement_source is what the contract settles on, in the venue's own words where published. source_published says whether the venue publishes that rule. needs_check marks rows Nick has not confirmed against a primary source; the page shows them as unverified. OpenMarket's own row is computed from src/lib/engine/dealer/rulebook.ts at render time and is not in this file.

rows.product: IPO-timing and valuation-threshold event contracts on OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe, Databricks and Kraken
rows.notes: The closest live comp to OpenMarket's quarterly binary. Resolution depends on a single third-party data provider; no public review of resolution quality has been published as of the as_of date. Threshold contracts on Volmex indices and HIP-3 open-interest markets are also listed.

rows.product: Binary valuation ladders (strike by valuation threshold and date) on Anthropic, Anduril, OpenAI, Databricks, Stripe, Figure and others; spot shares planned
rows.settlement_source: Not published for real money. Their own post on implied pricing flags Polymarket's dependency on Nasdaq Private Market marks.
rows.notes: Direct competitor on the same names. Their design essays argue for keeping binaries and rebuilding the order book with cross-rung netting. Funding and backers not disclosed. Settlement for live money is the open question.

rows.product: Long/short event contracts for professional traders, including markets on Anthropic and OpenAI that the team says trade like futures
rows.settlement_source: Not found in public materials as of the as_of date
rows.notes: Solana funds, offchain matching engine, 0.01 fee constant with a 50% maker rebate. Seed from Wintermute Ventures and DBA (Aug 2025), $9M Series A led by USV (Jul 2026). The founder has said insider trading on open venues is arguably price discovery.

rows.product: Pre-IPO perpetual futures on Hyperliquid (HIP-3), in units of valuation divided by one billion
rows.settlement_source: Hybrid oracle: a blend of secondary trades, priced rounds, mutual-fund marks, 409A valuations and comparables, mixed 50/50 with an 8-hour EMA of the venue's own mark; converts to a standard perp at IPO
rows.void_rule: None. Positions were settled by the venue at wind-down: OpenAI 1341.80, Anthropic 1618.90.
rows.notes: The oracle failure that defines the category: on 2026-05-28 the SpaceX perp fell about 45% in 30 minutes on bad offchain data, 484 users were liquidated for $1.74M and the venue compensated them. Cumulative volume about $650M, 11k traders. The founding team joined Phantom on 2026-06-30 to build wallet-native perps and private-market trading. The founder wrote that lab employees used the book to mark their own equity.

rows.product: IPO perpetuals on Hyperliquid without a pre-listing oracle; the Cerebras IPO perp is the cited case
rows.settlement_source: The IPO's opening public price; no oracle before listing, which limits the product to names with a near-term listing date
rows.notes: Pantera's June 2026 map reports the Cerebras perp settled within 3% of the open. trade.xyz co-signed the Hyperliquid Policy Center's August 2026 letter to the SEC proposing that pre-IPO perps list only inside a window after a public S-1 filing, with the oracle and settlement disclosed in advance.

rows.product: Pre-IPO perpetuals on Hyperliquid, starting with Anthropic
rows.settlement_source: Not found in public materials as of the as_of date
rows.notes: $14M seed led by Ribbit Capital (Aug 2026); team from Citadel, Optiver, Polymarket and Millennium. The nearest funded competitor on the same first name. No settlement rule located; fill in from their docs when they publish.

rows.product: Non-custodial front end routing to Hyperliquid, Lighter and Ostium; lists perps on OpenAI and Anthropic beside prediction-market positions
rows.settlement_source: Whatever the routed venue publishes; Liquid is a distributor, not a settlement venue
rows.notes: About $3B volume and 40k users by May 2026; $25.6M raised (Paradigm led the seed; Left Lane co-led the April 2026 extension). The founder cites the CFTC's Phantom no-action letter for not registering as a broker or exchange. A reference-price customer, not a comp.

rows.product: Trading front end for pre-IPO shares, equities, crypto and perpetuals with AI-generated trade ideas (YC F25)
rows.settlement_source: No published pricing methodology for the pre-IPO names it shows
rows.notes: Three to five people in New York; backed by YC, Inventum and Alliance. Founder is an ex-Jane Street, IMC and Akuna options trader. A reference-price customer.

rows.product: Planned CFTC-regulated perpetual futures on single-name public equities and indices under joint CFTC/SEC oversight
rows.settlement_source: Public equity prices; no private names proposed
rows.status: pre-launch; DCM and DCO applications planned
rows.notes: About $30M led by Lux Capital at about $300M (June 2026). The June 4, 2026 SEC Harmonization Initiative memo asks for a DCM license with an exemption to list perps on securities. The memo does not address a reference price for names with no spot market, which is the gap OpenMarket sits in.

rows.product: CFTC-regulated event contracts; BTCPERP approved May 2026; no private-company valuation contracts found
rows.settlement_source: Not applicable; Kalshi has no published settlement source for private-company valuations
rows.status: no private-name contracts as of the as_of date
rows.notes: The DCM a US listing would resemble. Kalshi's contract rules go through CFTC self-certification; its head of research has described the resolvability test on the record. A third-party reference price is what Kalshi would need to list these names.

context.item: Hyperliquid Policy Center letter to the SEC on pre-IPO perps (2026-08-18)
context.summary: Five pillars: classification, disclosures, listing eligibility only inside a window after a public S-1, phased access with leverage and position limits, market-integrity controls on deployer MNPI. Cites the SK Hynix oracle anomaly in which one trade moved a mark 18%.

context.item: Pantera, Tokenized Startups: Restoring Access to Pre-IPO Companies (2026-06-08)
context.summary: Maps Jarsy, Ventuals, PreStocks, trade.xyz, RVI and USVC. Flags Ventuals' oracle risk from unaudited valuation rumors, notes that Ventuals-style perps are security-based swaps barred from US retail, and that founders can void tokenized sales.
